title: Reconstructionist Judaism
hook: Mordecai Kaplan described Judaism as an evolving religious civilization

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: worldwide. Reform, Liberal, Progressive: one family, many names on many doors. Did you ask what something is called somewhere else? Today, a movement with one big idea in its name. Day one thousand two hundred thirty.

One shelf in a family's living room. A prayer book with a cracked spine. A cookbook with honey cake stains on the page for the new year. A record of old Yiddish songs. A Hebrew newspaper someone brought back from a trip. A history of the family's town that no longer exists. A pair of Shabbat candlesticks. Now the question. Which of these things is Judaism? Only the prayer book? Or the whole shelf? A teacher named Mordecai Kaplan gave an answer that started a movement.
screen: `ONE SHELF.` → `PRAYERS, RECIPES, SONGS, HISTORY.` → `WHICH OF THESE IS JUDAISM?`

segments.voice: Reconstructionist Judaism. Kaplan was a rabbi and a teacher, and his answer was: the whole shelf. He wrote that Judaism is not only a religion, a set of beliefs and rituals. It is a civilization: the whole life of a people, including its language, its land, its history, its literature, its art and music, its food, its customs and its law. Religion is at its heart, he said, but it is not the whole of it. His idea turns on three words. First, civilization. If Judaism is a civilization, then a Jew who sings the songs, studies the history, speaks Hebrew, or cooks the holiday foods is taking part in Jewish life, not standing outside it. Second, evolving. Civilizations change. They borrow, adapt and grow. Kaplan argued that Judaism has always done this, and has to keep doing it to stay alive. That is where the name comes from: each generation reconstructs the tradition for its own time, the way you might rebuild an old house, keeping the foundation and changing the rooms. Third, the people. Kaplan put the Jewish people at the center, the community that carries the civilization forward. A psalm pictures that handing-on: "One generation shall praise thy works to another, and shall declare thy mighty acts." One generation to another. Each one receives, and each one builds. Kaplan taught within the Conservative world for a long time, and Reconstructionism grew from his ideas into a movement of its own. Today's line names his picture: an evolving civilization.
screen: `NOT ONLY A RELIGION.` · `A CIVILIZATION: THE WHOLE SHELF.` · `EVOLVING: EACH GENERATION REBUILDS.` · `THE PEOPLE AT THE CENTER.` · then, large: `ONE GENERATION TO ANOTHER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: think of Judaism as a civilization. Settle, and breathe. Picture the shelf again. Let each thing on it come forward, one at a time: the prayer book, the recipe, the song, the language, the story of a town, the candlesticks. With each one, notice that it belongs to the same people. Then, if you like, turn to your own life. What would be on your shelf? Which things there carry a whole civilization? The bell holds the time.
Reconstructionist Judaism. The movement built on Mordecai Kaplan's idea that Judaism is an evolving religious civilization, rebuilt by each generation. Today's word.
Your line: an evolving civilization. Today, notice one thing you do that you inherited and changed a little: a recipe, a phrase, a holiday habit. Day one thousand two hundred thirty.

howItsDone: Reconstructionist Jews, following Mordecai Kaplan, treat Judaism as the evolving civilization of the Jewish people, so congregations embrace Jewish culture, language, history and arts alongside prayer and ritual.
